paper_reference.citation: N. Blinov et al., arXiv:2511.09619v2, JHEP 06 (2026) 155
paper_reference.important_distinction: The low-mass condition controls the explicit m_V^2/omega^2 correction; it does not by itself establish the separate nonrelativistic-muon and negligible-recoil assumptions. The B.17-weighted muon kinematic diagnostics and direct B.13/B.16 comparison test those assumptions independently.
paper_reference.quoted_mass_regime: The O(m_V^2/omega^2) term in the B.14 parenthesis is typically dropped for m_V less than or of order MeV.

scope_limits: Local source-rate comparison at r=0 and 12.5 km only.
No radial luminosity integral, escape probability, opacity, or transport calculation.
The 10 MeV result is reused from its previously validated output and is not recomputed.
No coupling, production, absorption, opacity, or stellar-profile rescaling.
The B.14 low-mass statement concerns dropping O(m_V^2/omega^2); nonrelativistic muon and negligible-recoil assumptions are tested separately.
No axial exclusion curve is produced; this scan is a pure-vector literature benchmark.
title: Low-mass exact moving-muon B.13 vs stationary exact recoil and B.14--B.16 vector scan
